evidence.title: Incident Report: False Hull-Integrity Recall
evidence.content: A welding-inspection telemetry fault triggered an emergency recall on a completed hull, timed to collapse a rival shipyard's steel-supply contract in favor of a Corvid-linked supplier. Chief inspector Han So-yeon is being blamed for the cost overrun.

evidence.title: Han So-yeon: Statement
evidence.content: "I flagged the telemetry as tampered three days before the recall went public. Nobody acted on my report. Then somehow I'm the one who gets blamed for the overrun."

evidence.title: Recall Press Release
evidence.content: Public statement announcing the emergency recall, citing "newly discovered" hull-integrity defects. See Media for the original scanned wire copy.

evidence.title: Sabotage Payload — Decrypted
evidence.content:
DECRYPTED TELEMETRY OVERRIDE

Payload injects false stress-fracture readings into the welding-inspection feed. File hash: TK-5F3C9A.

ANALYSIS: This is a deliberate injection, not sensor failure.

evidence.title: Forensics Registry Match
evidence.content: Hash Compare returns a registry hit: origin "Case 001 — Apapa resale-ledger toolkit," same encryption family. The same toolkit signature used to hide a stolen pallet's ledger is now hiding a fabricated structural defect.

chat.text: That wasn't theft or a leak. Someone built a fake crisis on purpose, for profit. That's a different animal.
Flagging this now — telemetry readings don't match a physical inspection I ran myself an hour ago. Something's wrong with the feed, not the hull.
Noted. Will escalate in the morning.
The recall already went public. Nobody escalated anything.

metadata.Note: Original scanned wire copy, contrast degraded

reveal.revealText: Wire timestamp, previously illegible: filed 02:50 — before the 03:12 inspection log entry the recall claims to be responding to.

TK-5F3C9A.payload: Shared encryption/injection toolkit. Same signature family as the resale ledger's decryption wrapper.

timeline.title: Recall Press Release Filed
timeline.text: Wire service receives the recall statement, timestamped before the defect it cites was logged.

timeline.title: Inspection Rig Photo Taken
timeline.text: Han So-yeon photographs the hull during a routine physical inspection — no defect visible.

timeline.title: Telemetry Anomaly Logged
timeline.text: Han flags a mismatch between physical inspection and telemetry feed.

timeline.title: Recall Already Public
timeline.text: Han learns the recall went out hours before her own report was ever escalated.

network.name: Rival Steel Contract
network.desc: The rival shipyard's steel-supply contract, collapsed by the recall's reputational damage.

network.name: Corvid-Linked Supplier
network.desc: Awarded the replacement contract within 48 hours of the recall — unusually fast for a contract this size.

suspects.name: Han So-yeon
suspects.notes: Initially blamed for the recall's cost overrun. Timeline shows the recall was filed before her own inspection entry — she couldn't have caused what predates her report.

suspects.name: Corvid-Linked Replacement Supplier
suspects.notes: Awarded the replacement contract within 48 hours of a recall built from a fabricated telemetry payload sharing Case 001's toolkit signature.

solution.successMessage: Han flagged the fault before it existed as a public crisis — the timeline alone proves the recall was written first and the "discovery" staged after. The toolkit hash closes the loop: the same signature that hid Case 001's stolen ledger built this fake disaster too.

onDocument.c5_ev05: First real registry hit. Not a hunch — a match. Someone's running the same toolkit across completely unrelated cases.

onThread.c5_thread02: She reported this before it was even a scandal. That's not the behavior of someone hiding sabotage.

onFlag.HASH_MATCHED: TK-5F3C9A. Apapa to Busan. That's not a coincidence anymore.

onBookmark.c5_ev04: Bookmarked. The payload hash is going to matter again — I can feel it.
